brief: Pictet's technical-views note argues the S&P 500's breakout above its wave-5 target was a false breakout, invalidating the bullish extension scenario and shifting the picture to a higher-degree wave-4 correction testing support at 6,817. Oversold momentum, a VIX near 36 and Nasdaq nearing support raise the odds of a tactical rebound, but breadth (46.0% of S&P 500 members above their 200-day SMA, only 5.57% at new 52-week lows) has not reached the capitulation levels of 2022 or April 2025, so a major bottom is unconfirmed. A five-wave count puts the S&P 500 in a potential wave-4 bounce toward 7,267–7,350 before a possible wave-5 decline. Europe is weakening but less advanced than the US: EURO STOXX 50 and DAX are testing 200-day SMA support, the CAC is more fragile, the SMI is retesting its breakout. Asian equities are corrective with rising dispersion; the Hang Seng has broken down toward 21,425 while the Nikkei's bullish RSI divergence suggests it may be closer to stabilising.
